intro.text: A religion of Sel which teaches that each person's personality is a gift to be enjoyed.
A religion centred in Teod, Sarene's homeland, and descended from the same parent religion as Shu-Dereth. It teaches that each person's personality is a gift to be enjoyed.

A sect of Shu-Keseg centred in Teod. Its reach has shrunk, and only Teod and Arelon still hold it as their official faith. It is a gentle, unassuming religion whose chapels are built to put worshippers at ease.

description.text: The Korathi worship Domi, a loving god often called Merciful Domi. The heart of the faith is the uniting power of love.
A Korathi teaching holds that unity can come out of strife.
The faithful should help those less fortunate than themselves.
The Korathi call Elantrian magic a sham, but their priests teach that the Elantrians, even since the Reod, are Domi's children and deserve respect and love.

The church seems to dislike seons for their tie to Elantris; its patriarch once threw Sarene's seon Ashe out of a Teo chapel. Raoden and Sarene, though, see seons as gifts from Domi, sent in love to protect, comfort and befriend.

items.text: Shu-Korath began when Korath, a student of Keseg, left JinDo to spread Shu-Keseg's central teaching, the unity of all mankind, holding that it should come about through love.
Korath's teachings took root in Teod, the faith's homeland.

Korath travelled to Arelon, whose people worshipped the Elantrians as living gods. Sure of their own divinity, the Elantrians let other faiths preach there, even inside Elantris, but Shu-Korath won few followers until the Reod, when the Arelene turned from Elantrians they saw as diseased or cursed.
To show respect, and friendship towards Teod, the Elantrians raised a grand Korathi chapel inside Elantris, reputed to be the finest of all Korathi chapels.
Raoden and his companions in Elantris made the chapel their home and the base of their work in the city.

The two sects differed on how to reach their shared goal of unity, but real conflict began only when Fjorden used Shu-Dereth to justify conquering its neighbours under the banner of divine unification. The number of nations with Shu-Korath as their official faith shrank, though people in those lands may still follow it.
Hrathen notes how far Shu-Korath has fallen: only two nations, Arelon and Teod, still follow it.
Ceremonies shaped by Elantrian culture, such as the Widow's Trial, are still expected of the Korathi, even though anything touching Elantris is taboo since the Reod.

Since the Reod, Korathi priests have readied those taken by the Shaod for Elantris: they wash them in water from the Aredel River, dress them in a white robe and give them a basket of bread, vegetables, grain and wine.
Korathi priests and devout followers wear pendants carved with Aon Omi, and such pendants are exchanged at Korathi weddings.
Sarene goes to a Korathi chapel in Kae to learn from its priest, Father Omin.
The church is led by a patriarch, a title held by Seinalan.
Priests lead the chapels, with a head priest named in each city. A group of leaders elects a new patriarch when one is needed.
